feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so it states no outcome for it. The candidate is the iteration 1 design (kp 2.0, base_speed 1.4, ki 0, last_direction, weights -2..2, sensors x -0.02..0.02 at y 0.04, sensor_size 0.012) with kd moved from 0.2 to 0.15. Iteration 1 is the best raced design (75.97), and iteration 6 reproduced it exactly, so the baseline is reliable. The change is valid and single-lever. Iteration 1 had steering_oscillation of 0.23 on the s-bend, which is the main jitter problem. Iteration 2 (kd 0.1) and iteration 3 (kd 0.1) both lost s-bend progress (0.29 to about 0.15), but both also changed base_speed or kp, so kd alone is not cleanly isolated. Iteration 3 also showed that kp 2.5 leaves max_error at 0.062 to 0.065, so kp is not the lever for the off-track failure. Read the race in this order. (1) If s-bend progress stays at or above about 0.25 and steering_oscillation falls below about 0.20, kd 0.15 is a better trade and the next test is base_speed. (2) If s-bend progress falls below about 0.22, the progress lost to kd is the limit, so return kd to 0.2, which kept progress in iteration 1, and do not lower kd further. (3) In either case, max_error will probably stay near 0.06 to 0.065 because bend reach, not gain, sets it. Approving this test is reasonable: it is the midpoint the team needs to check, and the race gives per-track telemetry for the next decision.
requested_changes: If s-bend progress stays at or above about 0.25 and steering_oscillation falls below about 0.20 with kd 0.15, keep kd 0.15 and test base_speed 1.5 in one step. Speed has only been lowered so far (iteration 2, base 1.2, cut s-bend progress from 0.29 to 0.155), so raising it is untested and may recover completion_time.
If s-bend progress falls below about 0.22 with kd 0.15, revert kd to 0.2, the value that held progress in iteration 1 (0.29 on the s-bend), and do not lower kd further.
Keep kp at 2.0. Iteration 3 (kp 2.5) left max_error at 0.062 to 0.065, so raising kp has not moved the off-track failure.
